proposals.before: He rose in due course to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.
proposals.after: He rose in due course to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not Grand Secretary (大學士).

proposals.before: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.
proposals.after: He was promoted in succession to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not Grand Secretary (大學士).

proposals.before: In his twentieth year of service he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.after: In the twentieth year he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: 二十年 after 乾隆七年 is Qianlong 20, not the twentieth year of Guangnai's service.

proposals.before: At the autumn assizes Guangnai argued that Chen Fu of Guangxi, who had killed a thief while guarding his standing grain after repenting of earlier wrongdoing, should not be classified as a capital case;
proposals.after: At the autumn assizes Guangnai argued that Chen Fuhui of Guangxi, a prisoner who had killed a thief while guarding his standing grain, should not be classified as a capital case;
proposals.reason: 陳父悔 is the prisoner's name; 父悔 is not a clause about repenting of earlier wrongdoing.

proposals.before: In the twenty-seventh year the Emperor judged Guangnai too rigid and impractical for the vice censorate and appointed him acting Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.
proposals.after: In the twenty-seventh year the Emperor judged Guangnai too rigid and impractical for the vice censorate and appointed him acting Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 署內閣學士 is acting Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not acting Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: After several months he indicated that Guangnai was merely dull and incompetent, without grave fault, and demoted him to left vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
proposals.after: After several months he indicated that Guangnai was merely dull and incompetent, without grave fault, and demoted him to Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
proposals.reason: 左授 marks downward appointment; 左 is not part of the title 通政司副使.

proposals.before: and also Provincial Administration Commissioner Sheng Zhu, who on his journey to the capital the previous year carried an suspiciously large sum of money, arousing gossip;
proposals.after: and also Provincial Administration Commissioner Sheng Zhu, who on his journey to the capital the previous year carried a suspiciously large sum of money, arousing gossip;
proposals.reason: English article error: 'an suspiciously' should be 'a suspiciously'.

proposals.before: The Emperor found Guangnai's receipts convincing. Agui had already returned to the capital, so Guangnai was sent back to Zhejiang to investigate impartially, with Jiangsu Governor Min E'yuan to join the trial and take Guangnai's testimony.
proposals.after: The Emperor found Guangnai's receipts convincing. Agui had already returned to the capital, so he was ordered back to Zhejiang to investigate impartially, with Jiangsu Governor Min E'yuan to join the trial and take Guangnai's testimony.
proposals.reason: Chinese 令復如浙江 follows 阿桂已還京師 and orders Agui, not Guangnai, to return to Zhejiang; Guangnai is the witness (以光鼐質證), not the commissioner sent back.

proposals.before: In his thirty-third year of service he was appointed investigating censor for the Henan circuit.
proposals.after: In the thirty-third year he was appointed investigating censor for the Henan circuit.
proposals.reason: 三十三年 continues Qianlong regnal dating from 乾隆二十二年, not a count of years in office; the literal English already has the correct sense.

proposals.before: The Emperor ordered a minister in Beijing to question Xibao and sent officials with him to search Quan's house; nothing was found, and Xibao admitted he had acted rashly.
proposals.after: The Emperor ordered the princes and ministers left in charge at the capital to summon Xibao and question him, and also ordered the metropolitan commandant to send officials with Xibao to inspect Quan's household; no trace was found, and Xibao confessed he had been rash.
proposals.reason: 王大臣 is the plural body of princes and high ministers left to manage the capital, not a single minister; 召…問狀 and 步軍統領遣官 are omitted in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: The Emperor ordered the minister in Beijing to summon Xibao and question him, and also ordered the metropolitan commandant to send officials with Xibao to inspect Quan's household; no trace was found, and Xibao confessed he had been rash.
proposals.after: The Emperor ordered the princes and ministers left in charge at the capital to summon Xibao and question him, and also ordered the metropolitan commandant to send officials with Xibao to inspect Quan's household; no trace was found, and Xibao confessed he had been rash.
proposals.reason: 留京辦事王大臣 is a plural collegial body, not “the minister in Beijing.”

proposals.before: Xibao was a nephew of Yishi Cong; for two generations the family served at court and was known for outspokenness.
proposals.after: Xibao was a nephew of Yishi; for two generations the family served at court and was known for outspokenness.
proposals.reason: 一士從子 means nephew of (Cao) Yishi; 從子 is the kinship term, not a personal name Cong fused onto Yishi.

proposals.before: Xibao was a nephew of Yishi Cong; for two generations the family served in the censorate and won fame for daring speech.
proposals.after: Xibao was a nephew of Yishi; for two generations the family served in the censorate and won fame for daring speech.
proposals.reason: The literal likewise treats 從子 as part of the uncle’s name; 從子 is “brother’s son.”

proposals.before: Inspecting southern grain transport, he found vessels blocked at Guazhou; Zhending prayed to the river god, the wind turned fair, and the fleet moved—people called it "Secretary Xie's wind."
proposals.after: Inspecting southern grain transport, he found vessels blocked at Guazhou; Zhending prayed to the god, the wind turned fair, and the fleet moved—people called it "Lord Xie's wind."
proposals.reason: 謝公 is an honorific “Lord/Master Xie,” not the office “Secretary.”

proposals.before: Inspecting the eastern city he seized a man driving an illegal carriage at speed—it was Heshen's brother-in-law. When the man was insolent, Zhending had him beaten and burned the carriage.
proposals.after: Inspecting the eastern city he seized a man driving an illegal carriage at speed—it was the younger brother of Heshen's concubine. When the man was insolent, Zhending had him beaten and burned the carriage.
proposals.reason: 妾弟 is the younger brother of a concubine (妾), not a generic brother-in-law of a principal wife.

proposals.before: While inspecting the eastern city he found someone driving an illegal carriage racing through the streets; he seized and questioned him—it was Heshen's wife's younger brother. He spoke insolently; Zhending ordered him beaten severely and burned the carriage.
proposals.after: While inspecting the eastern city he found someone driving an illegal carriage racing through the streets; he seized and questioned him—it was the younger brother of Heshen's concubine. He spoke insolently; Zhending ordered him beaten severely and burned the carriage.
proposals.reason: 妾 is concubine, not wife; 弟 is younger brother.

proposals.before: The Emperor praised Feng's honesty and promoted him to Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
proposals.after: The Emperor praised Feng's honesty and promoted him to Counselor of the Office of Transmission.
proposals.reason: Chinese 通政司參議 is distinct from later 通政司副使 in s0180; rendering both as Vice Commissioner collapses two offices.

proposals.before: The duty room inside the inner right gate lies close to the imperial residence; because audiences at the Hall of Mental Cultivation require advance preparation, an hour or two of lead time is needed.
proposals.after: The duty room inside the inner right gate lies close to the imperial residence; because audiences at the Hall of Mental Cultivation require advance preparation, one or two ke of lead time is needed.
proposals.reason: 一兩刻 is a ke (about a quarter-hour), not an English hour; the idiomatic version invents a longer interval.

proposals.before: At the Yuanming Garden, Heshen and Fu Chang'an should not remain only in the east-facing lodge south of Ruyi Gate, nor Wang Jie and Dong Gao only in the Southern Study lodge—I ask that these arrangements be corrected too."
proposals.after: At the Yuanming Garden, Heshen and Fu Chang'an stay only in the east-facing lodge south of the wall outside Ruyi Gate, and Wang Jie and Dong Gao stay only in the Southern Study lodge—I ask that these arrangements be corrected as well."
proposals.reason: 止於 reports current practice; the idiomatic text invents a hortative should-not that the Chinese does not state.

proposals.before: He rose through three promotions to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court, concurrently Vice Minister of Rites.
proposals.after: He rose through three promotions to Academician of the Grand Secretariat, concurrently Vice Minister of Rites.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is not 大學士; Grand Secretary of the Inner Court is the wrong office.

proposals.before: The Emperor said Zhuangtu had spoken from reckless imagination, yet this did not prevent taking slander as remonstrance; there was no need hastily to add grave punishment—he was demoted to left reader in the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.after: The Emperor said Zhuangtu had spoken from reckless imagination, yet this did not prevent taking slander as remonstrance; there was no need hastily to add grave punishment—he was demoted and appointed a reader in the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Leftward 左授 marks demotion, not an office named left reader; 內閣侍讀 is Grand Secretariat reader.

proposals.before: When a reader's post fell vacant he was made principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.after: Then, because reader posts were in short supply, he was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.reason: 侍讀缺少 means a shortage of reader posts, not a vacancy he filled as reader.

proposals.before: Soon, because a reader's post was vacant, he was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.after: Soon, because reader posts were lacking, he was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.reason: 缺少 here is shortage of reader posts, not a single vacancy.

proposals.before: I ask that twenty men be chosen from vice ministers, Hanlin, censors, governors, and prefects to serve in rotation inside the palace.
proposals.after: I beg that from among vice ministers, Hanlin officials, and censors at court, and provincial administration commissioners, judicial commissioners, circuit intendants, and prefects in the provinces, twenty men be carefully chosen to serve in rotation within the palace.
proposals.reason: 籓、臬、道、府 are provincial administration commissioners, judicial commissioners, circuit intendants, and prefects, not collapsed governors and prefects.

decisions.reason: 累遷內閣學士 names Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not Grand Secretary (大學士). The original inflates the office.
The same unit, 累遷內閣學士, is Academician of the Grand Secretariat. Literal Grand Secretary of the Inner Court is the wrong office.
二十年 is a bare regnal year, not years in Guangnai's service. The original invents “of service.”
廣西囚陳父悔 is the prisoner Chen Fuhui; 父悔 is his given name, not a clause about repenting of earlier wrongdoing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 廣西囚陳父悔守田禾殺賊

decisions.reason: 署內閣學士 is acting Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not acting Grand Secretary.
左授通政司副使 uses 左授 for a downward appointment; 左 is not part of the title 通政司副使.
The idiomatic English is ungrammatical: “an suspiciously” must be “a suspiciously.” The Chinese sense is otherwise unchanged.
After 阿桂已還京師, 令復如浙江 orders Agui back to Zhejiang; 以光鼐質證 makes Guangnai the witness, not the commissioner sent back.

decisions.reason: 留京辦事王大臣 is the collegial body of princes and ministers left in the capital; 召錫寶問狀 and 步軍統領遣官 are also in the Chinese and belong in the English.

decisions.reason: 留京辦事王大臣 is plural; “the minister in Beijing” wrongly makes it a single official.
一士從子 means Xibao was the brother's son of (Cao) Yishi; 從子 is kinship, not a given name Cong attached to 一士.
The literal likewise fuses 從子 into the uncle's name. 從子 is “brother's son.”
禱於神 is prayer to a god, not specifically a river god; 謝公風 is an honorific “Lord Xie,” not the office Secretary.

decisions.reason: 和珅妾弟 is the younger brother of Heshen's concubine, not a generic brother-in-law of a principal wife.
妾 is concubine, not wife; 弟 is younger brother. “Wife's younger brother” misreads both elements.
通政司參議 is Counselor of the Office of Transmission, distinct from 通政司副使 in the next promotion.

decisions.after: The duty room inside the inner right gate lies close to the imperial residence; because audiences at the Hall of Mental Cultivation require advance preparation, a quarter-hour or two of lead time is needed.
decisions.reason: 一兩刻 is one or two ke (about a quarter-hour each), not English hours. The proposal is right on the unit but “ke” is not natural idiomatic English.
止於 states where Heshen, Fu Chang'an, Wang Jie, and Dong Gao currently stay; the original invents a hortative “should not remain.” The Chinese also specifies 如意門外南順牆.

decisions.reason: 三遷至內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not Grand Secretary (大學士).

claimRetractions.reason: The personal-name value Yishi Cong was produced only by reading 從子 as part of the uncle's name; 一士 does not include Cong.

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name must be Chen Fuhui for 陳父悔; Chen Fu came from splitting 父悔 as a repentance clause.
謝公 is an honorific Lord Xie, not the office title Secretary Xie.

claimRevisions.reason: The popular epithet 謝公風 should be rendered Lord Xie's wind, matching the honorific 公.
The descriptive kinship 和珅妾弟 is the younger brother of Heshen's concubine, not a generic brother-in-law.
